rows: Employers must provide welfare facilities and a working environment that is healthy and safe.
Workplace buildings should be kept in good repair.
Workplaces and equipment must be maintained so they remain safe and work efficiently.
Dangerous defects should be corrected promptly or people protected from the risk.
Open edges and floor openings require suitable measures to prevent falls.
Workplaces need enough space for safe movement and access.
Floors, corridors and stairs should be kept free from obstructions.
Suitable drainage is required where wet processes could create risk.
The Workplace Regulations apply to most, but not every, type of workplace.
Public property records cannot verify current housekeeping, maintenance, access, welfare or temporary hazards.
Safety recalls can apply to vehicles, components, tyres, child seats and other vehicle accessories.
Manufacturers normally notify registered keepers when a vehicle is recalled for safety reasons.
Safety-recall repairs or replacement parts are not usually charged to the owner.
Owners can check outstanding safety recalls using official services.
A serious safety defect is generally a design or manufacturing issue likely to cause injury or death and occurring without warning.
Serious safety defects should first be reported to the manufacturer.
DVSA can investigate where the manufacturer response is unsatisfactory.
Vehicle owners remain responsible for keeping vehicles safe to drive.
A model-level recall does not prove that a particular vehicle is affected or remains unrepaired.
Vehicle-level conclusions require registration, make, model, year, VIN or recall-completion evidence as applicable.
Local authorities inspect food businesses and assign food-hygiene ratings.
In England, Wales and Northern Ireland ratings range from 0 to 5.
Inspections consider safe food handling, storage and preparation.
Inspections also consider premises cleanliness and condition.
Food-safety management processes and training form part of the rating assessment.
Businesses can appeal, publish a right-to-reply or request re-rating under scheme procedures.
The official search service holds rating information on behalf of local authorities.
Queries about an individual business should be directed to the relevant local authority.
A food-hygiene rating is not a measure of food quality.
Ratings describe the position at the last inspection and may not reflect later operational changes or temporary upload delays.
A food incident involves actual or suspected food or feed safety or quality concerns requiring consumer-protection action.
Unsafe or non-compliant food should be withdrawn from the supply chain promptly.
A recall is required where unsafe product has reached consumers or animal owners.
Businesses should notify the relevant local authority or port health authority.
Traceability information is needed to identify affected suppliers, customers, products and batches.
Consumer recall communications should identify the product, hazard and required action.
Unsafe product should be segregated, labelled and disposed of safely.
After the immediate response, root-cause analysis should identify preventive actions.
A general recall notice does not prove that a product is present at a particular premises.
Local conclusions require product, batch, date, distribution and traceability matching.
